doc.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Advice to jazz students about making a living in the pandemic
summary: Butch is unsure what to tell students but sees necessity breeding new ideas; he adds that normal will not return, as he lives with his lung transplant.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Yeah. What do you tell your, with jazz majors, what do you advise to them as far as post- graduation and making a living?

Swing or I’ll kill you. No, no, it’s just old jokes, sorry. Old musicians will remember that old joke. It’s like Joe Morello told me one time, he said, “A lot of times you can’t remember how many bars there are to a tune, but the old musicians can remember how many tunes there are to a bar” and I left my cowbell down on the campus, God-dog it.

Things were a little bit different before March of this year. You could still tour. You could work around the country. You could get gigs. There were some nice gigs. There were studios to be had where you could be on call. Not like the old, old days where you could make a good living being in the studio recording like let’s say the Wrecking Crew out in L.A. when they’d get all those huge hits so many years ago out in California. But there’s still a lot of work out there. And I say that in the past tense because now you can’t go anywhere and you can’t play anywhere due to the situation, the medicinal situation and the infections and the pandemic. So I’m not exactly sure what to tell the guys, the

kids, the men and women who come through my classes and take lessons and study with me. I’m not sure what’s going to happen. But this is a new age, this is a new time, and this is something that you can be very worried about and at the same time you can really charge ahead full steam because this sounds like this is the dawning of the Age of Aquarius. You’ve got to come up with something new and something fresh, and some way to make a living and some way to play music in order to just get it done. So creative minds are going to be coming up with some incredibly brilliant things that we never had to think of before. And I think it’s because it’s necessity. We have to in order to play music and sustain making a living. They are going to come up with some wild things to do and wonderful ways to do it. I just don’t know what it is yet. I’m as big a fan of all the guys who are thinking all of this stuff up as anybody else. One thing I’ve noticed is that some of the great musicians have a working situation where they’re not all piled on top of each other, like in a small club. They’ve got distancing and they wear masks, except when maybe a wind instrument, a saxophone or a trumpet or trombone or something is playing, and you get together for small concerts. An hour concert, an hour and a half concert. And you can donate by way of personal checks or by credit cards or PayPal or some other things. And some people are doing fairly well right now, at least continuing to play and make a little bit of money, but it’s going to go a different way and I just don’t know where. And I’m going to be very excited to see what the young minds today are going to come up with.
